title: Introduce invocation bucketizer and cross-tenant SLO explorer
author: Maya R. Singh
description: Context: alert noise from per-invocation token cost and latency spikes is creating high pager fatigue and long MTTR for long-tail cases. Motivation: reduce alert storming by grouping invocations into operationally useful buckets and provide a lightweight cross-tenant SLO explorer for root-cause and impact analysis without expensive full-trace hydration. What this PR does: 1) adds an invocation bucketizer that groups invocations by prompt-shape fingerprint, initial KV-warm state, model-variant tag, and inferred phase composition (generation vs rerank). Buckets are emitted as low-cardinality labels (invocation_bucket_id, bucket_reason) suitable for rollup counters and histograms; 2) instruments a compact bucket histogram metric (invocation_bucket_histogram) and a sampled bucket exemplar anchor that links to a short trace id for deep-dive; 3) introduces a new SLO Explorer dashboard JSON (observability/slo-explorer) with cross-tenant selectors, bucket-level aggregation, burn-rate overlays, and a lightweight diff mode to compare two time ranges or two tenants; 4) tightens sampling: we add a bucket-aware reservoir sampler that increases retention probability for underrepresented buckets to avoid masking rare but high-cost shapes; 5) adds docs and a migration guide for downstream alert rules to use bucketed rollups and avoid cardinality blowups. Rollout plan: feature flags are gated per-tenant; initial rollout to internal staging then 10 pilot tenants for 2 weeks; enable UI via feature-flagged console toggle; alert rule migration guidance provided in docs. Backwards compatibility: labels are additive; no change to existing per-invocation metrics. Performance: bucketizer code runs in the telemetry subservice, optimized for O(1) processing path with lock-free map for bucket table and async exemplar enrichment. Testing: unit tests for bucket mapping, e2e config in perf-canary, and a small replay bench to validate histogram semantics across sequence lengths. Risks and mitigations: cardinality spike — mitigated by explicit TTL and cardinality cap on bucket table; sampling bias — mitigated by reservoir uplift for low-volume buckets and a calibration job. Observability: new metrics emitted: telemetry.invocation_bucket_count, telemetry.invocation_bucket_histogram, telemetry.bucket_exemplar_trace, telemetry.bucket_warm_rate. Dashboards: slo-explorer.json, bucket-rollup-metrics.json. Migration notes: existing alerting playbooks updated to prefer bucketed 95/99p rollups with fallthrough to invocation-level when necessary. Related work: builds on ENG-1203 (adaptive sampling) and references PM-210 for tenant SLO UX. Deployment: automated helm chart patch (redwood-helm-charts) and feature flag in console. Merge method: squash.

review_comments: Ethan Park: overall looks solid. Please add a brief benchmark of per-invocation tail latency overhead when bucketizer is enabled; worried about p99 on hot paths.
Maya (author): added lightweight microbench in bucket_table_test.go showing ~200ns/op overhead in optimized path, included results in PR description.
Lucia Moreno: cardinality safety is critical. Can we add a hard cap metric for number of active buckets and an alert when exceeded?
Maya (author): added telemetry.bucket_table_active_gauge and a dashboard alert that triggers at 80% of cap, included migration note to throttle new bucket creation for noisy tenants.
Samir Patel: sampling uplift approach is interesting; please document bias implications and add a calibration job as a cron in perf-canary.
Maya (author): added perf-canary replay and a calibration job script under perf-canary/replays, tests show uplift reduces false-negative rate on rare heavy-cost shapes by ~45%.
Ethan Park: CI failed initially due to a vet error; re-ran and green after fix. Approving for squash-merge.
Lucia Moreno: small nits in console component (prop typing) fixed in follow-up commit. Approved.
release_notes: Add invocation bucketizer and SLO Explorer: introduces low-cardinality invocation buckets, compact histograms, exemplar anchors, and a new SLO Explorer dashboard. Feature-flagged rollout and migration guide included. Improves alert fidelity and reduces noise for long-tail invocation patterns.
